    $method = 'resume';

<?php
class ArrayStartPayload367 {
    public function __destruct() {
        global $weak;
        echo 'D', (int)($weak->get() === null), '|';
    }
}
function abruptArrayStart367() {
    global $pair;
    $pair = null;
    echo 'A|';
    throw new Exception('argument');
}
$target = new Fiber(static function () {
    try { Fiber::suspend('Y'); }
    finally { echo 'F|'; }
});
$weak = WeakReference::create($target);
echo $target->start(), '|';
$pair = [$target, 'start'];
unset($target);
try { $pair(new ArrayStartPayload367(), abruptArrayStart367()); }
catch (Exception $error) { echo $error->getMessage(), '|'; }
echo (int)($weak->get() === null), '|';
$target = new Fiber(static function () {
    try { Fiber::suspend('Y'); }
    finally { echo 'F|'; }
});
$weak = WeakReference::create($target);
echo $target->start(), '|';
$pair = [$target, 'start'];
unset($target);
try { $pair(first: new ArrayStartPayload367(), second: abruptArrayStart367()); }
catch (Exception $error) { echo $error->getMessage(), '|'; }
echo (int)($weak->get() === null);
engine_derived_expectation: A throwing argument retires the last selector while the pending ordinary start still owns its receiver and earlier payload. Positional versus extra-named payload destructors observe the real Zend argument/receiver unwind order; the handler never enters and no undefined return is read.
